moduleTitle: Advanced reporting insights in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Use the TestOps Dashboard to monitor team activity and quality trends beyond a single test run.
Interpret metrics such as average durations and team activity alongside pass rate and failure types.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Beyond a single run: the Insights dashboard

elements.description: Part of the broader Insights area, giving a higher-level view than the Reports tab alone — pulling together quality and activity signals so a team lead or consultant can answer 'how healthy is this project right now' without digging through individual test runs.

Interpreting pass rates, failure types, average durations, and team activity together — not in isolation — is what surfaces genuine trends and problem areas. A single metric (say, pass rate) read alone can mask a real issue that only shows up when cross-referenced with, say, a spike in average duration or a specific failure type.

bulletPoints: The TestOps Dashboard is the project-health view, broader than one report or one run.
Read pass rate, failure types, durations, and activity together — not any single metric in isolation.

elements.title: TestOps Dashboard panes
items: Remote Execution Runs — passed/failed remote runs (suite/plan/scheduled/labeled), filterable to Last 24 Hours / 3 Days / 7 Days, with failure reasons and frequency.
Test Overview — distributes all project tests across 5 statuses: Active, Quarantine, Evaluating, Draft, Flaky.
Duplication Level — the auto-grouping duplication score (lower = healthier).
Recent Activity — an activity log with links straight to the affected test/object.
Pull Requests — Pending / Requested Changes / Approved counts; only shown when the MASTER branch is selected.

elements.text: The 'Assigned to me' toggle filters every pane down to the current user's own activity/tests — EXCEPT Duplication Level, which stays project-wide regardless of the toggle.

bulletPoints: Test Overview's 5 statuses: Active, Quarantine, Evaluating, Draft, Flaky.
Pull Requests pane only appears when the master branch is selected.
'Assigned to me' filters everything except Duplication Level.

examPitfalls.title: Judging project health from pass rate alone
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Concluding a project is healthy purely because the pass rate looks fine, without checking duration trends or team activity.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Interpret pass rate, failure types, average durations, and team activity together — a stable pass rate can still hide a creeping duration regression or shrinking test coverage from reduced team activity.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the TestOps Dashboard provide that a single test run's result does not?

options.text: A higher-level view of project quality and team activity trends over time.
The ability to edit test steps directly.
A replacement for the CLI.
Nothing additional — it shows the same information as a single run.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's about project health over time, not one run's outcome.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The TestOps Dashboard gives a higher-level, project-wide view of quality and activity trends, letting you assess overall project health rather than reading one test run's isolated result.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why should pass rate, failure types, average durations, and team activity be interpreted together rather than individually?

options.text: Because Testim only displays one metric at a time.
Because a single metric read in isolation can mask a real problem that only shows up when cross-referenced with the others.
Because they are all exactly the same underlying number.
There's no benefit — any one metric alone tells the full story.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about a stable pass rate hiding a duration regression.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A stable pass rate can hide a creeping issue — like rising average durations or shrinking team activity/coverage — that only becomes visible when the metrics are read together instead of one at a time.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the TestOps Dashboard's Test Overview pane, which five status categories does it distribute tests across?

options.text: Active, Quarantine, Evaluating, Draft, Flaky
Passed, Failed, Skipped, Blocked, Pending
Draft, Active, Archived, Deleted, Locked
Green, Yellow, Red, Blue, Grey

practiceQuiz.hint: These are the same test-status concepts covered in the Test Library module, minus one addition.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Test Overview distributes all project tests across five statuses: Active (ready/stable), Quarantine (unstable), Evaluating (stability uncertain), Draft (in-progress), and Flaky (intermittently failing).

practiceQuiz.scenario: When does the Pull Requests pane appear on the TestOps Dashboard?

options.text: Always, regardless of which branch is selected.
Only when the master branch is selected.
Only on the free plan.
Only during an active CLI run.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's tied to one specific branch.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Pull Requests pane, showing Pending / Requested Changes / Approved counts, only appears on the dashboard when the master branch is the one selected.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the 'Assigned to me' toggle do on the TestOps Dashboard?

options.text: Deletes all data not assigned to the current user.
Filters every pane except Duplication Level down to the current user's own activity/tests.
Filters only the Duplication Level pane.
Switches to a completely different, non-filterable dashboard.

practiceQuiz.hint: One pane deliberately stays project-wide no matter what.
practiceQuiz.rationale: 'Assigned to me' filters all the dashboard's panes down to the current user's own activity — except Duplication Level, which always reflects the whole project regardless of the toggle.

quickRecap.value: Project-wide quality/activity view, broader than a single run's result.
Pass rate + failure types + durations + team activity — not any one metric alone.
Only shown when the master branch is selected.
